ai.description: The Arunachal pitviper is a medium-sized snake reaching 75 cm. It is dark green with faint crossbands and a distinct, prominent reddish-brown stripe along the sides of the head and body.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus arunachalensis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, dark-brown, diamond-shaped dorsal blotches that are bordered by a thin, pale yellow line.
ai.habitat: The Arunachal pit viper inhabits the dense, humid tropical evergreen forests of Arunachal Pradesh, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,700 meters.
ai.behavior: The Arunachal pitviper is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours hunting for small mammals and frogs within the dense, humid forests of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus arunachalensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of approximately 10 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus arunachalensis* is endemic to the West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh, India, occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 1,700 meters.
